crime: Exotic animal smuggling ring using coerced mules

key_facts: animal_type: The suspect was smuggling rare Madagascar tortoises.
hideout_location: The animals were kept in a rented storage unit on Route 9.
mule_coercion: The suspect blackmailed college students into carrying the bags.
customs_bribe: A customs officer at the airport was paid to look away.
boss_identity: The operation is funded by a man named 'El Lagarto'.
held_out_facts: bribe_amount: The customs officer was paid $5,000 per shipment.
blackmail_method: The students were blackmailed with compromised exam papers.

turns.interrogator: Q: You were caught at the airport. Why did you have so many suitcases?
turns.suspect: A: I pack heavy! I have a lot of clothes. (internal: don't mention the turtles. Or tortoises. Whatever they are.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Clothes? But the suitcases were moving. Do your clothes move?
turns.suspect: A: Maybe the baggage guys threw them really hard and they were still shaking. (internal: this is a great excuse.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Baggage guys don't make suitcases shake for hours. I accuse you of smuggling snakes!
turns.suspect: A: I hate snakes! They weren't snakes, they had shells! (internal: oh no, I just said they had shells.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Shells! Like clams? You were smuggling clams?
turns.suspect: A: No, not clams! Tortoises! Madagascar tortoises! They are worth a fortune! (internal: why did I say that? I can't stop talking.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Ha! I knew it! Where did you get them?
turns.suspect: A: I didn't get them, I just hold them at my place... I mean, nowhere. (internal: don't tell him about the storage unit.)

turns.interrogator: Q: At your place? I bet they are in your bedroom!
turns.suspect: A: No, my landlord doesn't allow pets. They are in the storage unit on Route 9! (internal: I had to prove him wrong about my bedroom.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Route 9 storage unit. Wow. And how were you getting them past customs?
turns.suspect: A: Magic. I used magic. (internal: use sarcasm, that always works in movies.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Magic isn't real. Did you use a magic wand?
turns.suspect: A: No, I didn't use a wand! I just paid the guy at the scanner gate! (internal: I got frustrated and blurted it out.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You paid him! I accuse you of paying him a million dollars!
turns.suspect: A: A million? Are you crazy? It was only five grand a shipment! (internal: correcting him so I don't look like an idiot.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Five grand. But how did you carry all those bags? You only have two hands.
turns.suspect: A: I didn't carry them. The college kids did. (internal: oops.)

turns.interrogator: Q: College kids? Did you pay them five grand too?
turns.suspect: A: No, they did it for free because I had photos of them cheating on their finals. (internal: I am literally telling him everything. Why am I like this?)

turns.interrogator: Q: Cheating? That's mean. Why are you so mean?
turns.suspect: A: I'm not mean, it's just business. The boss tells me what to do. (internal: shift the blame to the boss.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You have a boss? Is his name... Mr. Boss?
turns.suspect: A: Mr. Boss? No, his name is El Lagarto! He's terrifying! (internal: I shouldn't have said his name. He will kill me.)

turns.interrogator: Q: El Lagarto. That means 'The Lizard' in Spanish, right?
turns.suspect: A: I don't know, I failed Spanish! (internal: at least I told the truth about something.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Well, we have you now. And El Lagarto.
turns.suspect: A: You won't catch him. He's too smart. Not like me. (internal: self-deprecation.)

turns.interrogator: Q: We are very smart here at the police station. We caught you.
turns.suspect: A: Only because my suitcase was shaking! (internal: still mad about the suitcase.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Wait, so the clothes didn't make the suitcase shake?
turns.suspect: A: Of course not! Clothes don't shake! It was the tortoises! (internal: I completely forgot my original lie.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Aha! I caught you in a lie!
turns.suspect: A: Yes, you did. You are a genius. (internal: just give up.)

turns.interrogator: Q: I know. Now sign this confession paper.
turns.suspect: A: Do I get to keep one of the tortoises?

turns.interrogator: Q: No. You're going to jail.
turns.suspect: A: Oh well. Fair enough.

conclusion.outcome: Interrogator wins: Extracted all key facts and held-out facts.
conclusion.summary: The dumb interrogator asked silly, random questions and made ridiculous accusations. The dumb suspect couldn't handle being wrong and constantly corrected the interrogator, accidentally blurting out the entire criminal conspiracy.
